passage:
A famous leader's letter was displayed in a museum. Visitors gathered around the glass case to read it.
The handwriting was uneven, and some words were crossed out. A student was surprised. She had expected important historical documents to look perfect.
The guide explained that the crossed-out words showed the writer thinking, changing, and trying again.
The student liked the letter more after that. It made the leader seem human.
History often presents finished speeches and final decisions. Drafts show the struggle behind them. A crossed-out word can remind us that important ideas are shaped, not born perfect.
